impact: When a review fails because a Codex CLI internal subsystem (e.g., codex_core::memories::phase1, which hardcodes gpt-5.1-codex-mini) hits a model-unsupported error, our classifier extracts the offending model name correctly from the raw error, but the "Fall back to gpt-5.4" tip is hardcoded and doesn't consider whether the user is ALREADY on gpt-5.4 (or on a completely different model than the extracted failing one). Users see "Fall back to gpt-5.4 by setting \"model\": \"gpt-5.4\" in .reviewbridge.json" when they've already configured gpt-5.4 and the actual failure is from a Codex internal model they cannot reach. The extracted model name in the error message is also confusing — it names a model the user never configured. Reproduced via real debug session on 2026-04-23: review configured for gpt-5.4 failed because Codex CLI's memory-writing agent fired a separate call using gpt-5.1-codex-mini (hardcoded in the Rust binary) and that specific model is unavailable on ChatGPT-subscription tier. Related to ISS-001 in shape — classifier surfacing an unhelpful hint because it lacks context about which layer the model name came from.
resolution:
Mitigated by SDK bump in commit 306b4c1 (1.0.0 release): the bundled CLI moved from 0.104.0 to 0.128.0, which no longer exhibits the memory-agent gpt-5.1-codex-mini failure path against ChatGPT-tier auth — the misleading tip stops appearing in the most common scenario.

Classifier fix (T-032): classifyError's MODEL_ERROR branch now detects when the rejected model name differs (case-insensitively) from the model the review actually sent (context.model = resolvedModel). In that case it returns a distinct message — 'Model "<extracted>" was rejected, but the review ran with "<sent>" — the failure came from a Codex-internal call ... Changing "model" in .reviewbridge.json will not fix this. Try updating the Codex CLI/SDK, using API-key auth, or the Gemini backend.' — instead of the unhelpful change-your-model tip. Code stays ErrorCode.MODEL_ERROR (failover eligibility unchanged) and the 'Original error:' suffix is preserved (ISS-001 contract). The extracted===sent and extracted-absent paths keep the existing tips verbatim. Guard requires both names present and case-insensitively different, so a legitimately-bad user-configured model (which resolveModel forwards verbatim, making extracted===sent) still gets the generic tip — no false positives. Covered by 3 new + 1 realigned unit test in src/backends/codex.test.ts; full gate green.
title: MODEL_ERROR tip misleads when failure is from Codex internal subsystem (not caller's model)
